Hey guys, I know I talked about loving your neighbor and keeping the commandments , but just know that what matters most is the I shed for you. Does this make any sense?

And to make it even clearer: in a century Nazarene liturgical text called the Didache, which means “ teaching of the 12,” the Last Supper is depicted as the consumption of bread in memory of how Jesus multiplied the loaves and fed everyone. And the blood was to honor the fact that Jesus came from the line of David. So, this was a celebration of the fact that Yeshua was truly the Davidic Messiah for his early Nazarene followers. So this doctrine of blood atonement was clearly not invented by Jesus. was gradually built by various authors over several decades. Each of them imposed more and more sacrificial theology on the original passage.

But the most public act of Jesus' ministry was his cleansing of the temple. He entered the center of the Jewish sacrificial system, overturned the tables of the money changers, drove the animals out of their cages, and stopped the whole thing. In doing so, he quoted two prophets, Isaiah and Jeremiah, saying: “My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations.” "This is from Isaiah." "And you have turned it into a den of robbers." Jeremiah 7:11. But the word for “ robbers” in the Hebrew text of Jeremiah is “paritz,” which means murderers, destroyers, or cruel people. So it was precisely this word that the historical Jesus used in the temple. Only Hebrew was spoken in the temple especially when quoting Scripture, as Jesus does here.

And Jesus is clearly condemning the sacrificial system. So what the historical Jesus actually said and how the Jews in the temple heard it was: "You have turned my Father's house into a den of murder or violence." This is clearly not a person who believed in the sacrificial system. This was a man who wanted to dismantle it in front of everyone and was willing to give his life as a ransom for this cause. And twice in the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus quotes passage in the entire Bible. Hosea 6:6, which says: “ Go and learn what this means.” I want mercy, not sacrifice. "Knowing God , not burnt offerings." The clear context of Hosea 6:6 concerns animal sacrifice.

It was impossible to miss it. And Yeshua literally tells them: “ Turn back and see.” You missed something. God does not want this sacrifice. God wants mercy, repentance, and a humble and contrite heart." This is a direct rejection of the entire sacrificial apparatus around which Paul's theology is built. But perhaps the most explosive evidence comes from one of the oldest sources of Jesus' sayings, called the Hebrew Gospel of Matthew, which was Nazarenes. And more than a dozen church fathers, literally the entire elite of that time agreed that the first written Gospel was created by the disciple Matthew himself in Hebrew Judeo-Christians.

This means that Matthew, as we know, was a tax collector, and therefore he was literate enough to keep tax records, but he probably had a full bookish education. So he is the most likely of the 12 disciples who could have Gospel text. And we have 48 quotes preserved from this source. And in one of them, Jesus utters these words. I have come sacrifice. And until you stop offering sacrifices, the wrath of God will not turn away from you.

And Eusebius, the father of church history, clearly records that Jesus did not institute sacrifices, but considered them vile and humiliating, completely unworthy of the immortal nature of God. So even the church historian acknowledged that Jesus opposed the sacrificial system as a principle. So let's summarize. Jesus cleansed the temple to destroy the sacrificial system and put an end to it. He quoted Hosea 6:6 twice. And the early followers of Jesus preserved the statement where Jesus directly commanded them sacrifice.

And the earliest accounts of the Last Supper contain no mention of the forgiveness of sins or substitutionary atonement. These sayings were added later by other authors. But the entire premise of Paul's revolves around the idea that Jesus was God's last ritual blood sacrifice, slaughtered on the cross to atone for your sins. I don't think anyone here would disagree that Paul's entire gospel structure depends on the model of blood atonement. And yet, as we have just seen, the model of blood atonement was clearly not the gospel of Jesus. This is the gospel of Paul, or "my gospel," as Paul called it, which was adopted by Roman Catholic Church fathers and then introduced into the gospels by Greek editors and theologians.

This is not a conspiracy theory. This is what leading textual scholars demonstrate. And so the question that every Christian must wrestle with on this topic is : if Jesus came to abolish sacrifice, why did he want to become God's bloody sacrifice? If God truly desires mercy, not sacrifice, as the Bible says, why would God require sacrifice in human history from the holiest man in history to forgive your sins? Why did Jesus forgive sins long before he was crucified? And if the oldest sources do not contain this teaching, who inserted it there and why?

I think the answers to these questions are more obvious than most Christians are willing to admit. And that's okay. I myself have felt uncomfortable about this topic for quite some time. But the question is where does this lead us? I think this leaves us with a simple choice. You can continue to follow the theology of a person who never walked with Jesus, who admits to lying and impersonating others, who uttered false prophecy in the name of the Lord, who was given a demon that she could not cast out, and who was rejected by Jesus’ original followers.

Or you can simply go back to the source, to the scarlet letters, to the true teachings of the one you call Lord and Savior. 2 John 1:9 clearly states, "Whoever does not abide in the teaching of the Messiah does not have God. Whoever abides in the teaching of the Messiah has both the Father and the Son." The teachings of the Messiah, not the teachings of Paul, not the teachings of the church fathers or the Nicene Creed , but the teachings of Yeshua the Nazarene. Whether Jesus is the second person of the Trinity or not, whether he existed before birth or not, whether he is literally God in the flesh or not—none of this is mentioned by Jesus himself, none of this is given as a criterion for salvation. The teachings of Yeshua the Nazarene are what we must build our salvation on, for Jesus truly showed us the perfect way to God. He came to be a an example, and a guide, as he was called.

And that is why his followers followers of the Way . They followed the path that Jesus showed them, not fancy theological ideas and beliefs about him. So I'm not asking you to take my word for it in all of this. I'm just giving you some suggestions and food for thought. I would advise you to read the Gospels carefully, without imposing on them the prism of Pauline theology, and to ask yourself one simple question. Can I find any Pauline theology in the Gospels of Luke or Matthew?

If I had only this Gospel, would I have received from it the Christianity I profess today? If the answer is yes, then you obviously have nothing to worry about. But if the answer is no , then the question arises: what are you going to do about it? And I would advise you to simply return to the original words of the Master so that you may follow the path of Jesus, for the words of Jesus are sufficient for
